title: TCP Top Power Out-of-Range ANOMALY Response
procedure_steps: 1. Do NOT abort the in-progress wafer — the STOP button only prevents additional wafers from loading; the current wafer will complete its step. 2. Note the exact tcp_top_pwr reading, step number, wafer ID, and lot ID. 3. If tcp_top_pwr > 360 W (above max): notify process engineer immediately via fab pager. Place current lot on HOLD. 4. If tcp_top_pwr < 334 W (below min): notify process engineer. Mark wafer for re-inspection before resist strip. 5. After wafer completes: do NOT load additional wafers. Press STOP to pause cassette loading. 6. Check RF generator hour counter on the Maintain/TCP page. If hours > 1200, initiate PM work order immediately. 7. Check recipe version loaded against the approved master recipe sheet. A version mismatch is the most common cause of a ±10 W offset. 8. Check cooling water flow indicator on the TCP generator panel. Low flow triggers power derating. 9. If deviation > 30 W or 3+ consecutive wafers affected: escalate to process engineer per SOP-ESC-001. 10. Log incident in the fab MES with sensor value, step, and lot ID before resuming production.
safety_requirements: BCl3 and Cl2 process gases remain active during response — do NOT open chamber. Verify exhaust flow indicator is GREEN before approaching the tool. No LOCKOUT required while tool is in run state; LOCKOUT required only if chamber entry is needed.

title: TCP Top Power TREND Response — Approaching Limit
procedure_steps: 1. Log trend alert with current tcp_top_pwr value, direction (rising/falling), step number, and estimated time to breach. 2. Pull RF generator hour counter from Maintain/TCP page. If hours > 1100, schedule PM within the current production shift. 3. Review the last 5 wafers for power drift pattern. If drift rate exceeds 5 W per wafer, treat as ANOMALY and escalate to SOP-TCP-001. 4. Check impedance matching network auto-tune log. Increasing tune frequency indicates generator degradation. 5. Notify process engineer of trend. Engineer will decide whether to continue lot or pull tool for PM. 6. If lot is continued: increase inspection sampling to 100% for wafers in this lot. 7. Document tcp_top_pwr trend values in the run log with timestamp for maintenance records.
safety_requirements: Standard fab PPE required. No chamber entry. BCl3/Cl2 exhaust system must remain active throughout response.

title: BCl3 Flow Out-of-Range ANOMALY Response
procedure_steps: 1. Do NOT open chamber. BCl3 (boron trichloride) is toxic and reacts violently with moisture — inhalation hazard even at ppm levels. 2. Check bcl3_flow reading: normal range is 740–765 sccm. 3. If flow > 765 sccm: excess BCl3 increases etch rate and may over-etch metal lines. Place lot on HOLD. Notify process engineer. 4. If flow < 740 sccm: insufficient BCl3 reduces oxide breakthrough; aluminum etch may stall. Stop cassette loading. 5. Check MFC setpoint on the gas panel screen — recipe may have loaded an incorrect set-point. Compare loaded recipe to approved master. 6. Check upstream BCl3 cylinder pressure at the gas cabinet. If pressure < 50 psi, cylinder is near empty. Switch to backup cylinder per gas changeover SOP. 7. If recipe and cylinder are correct, MFC recalibration is required. Log PM request for BCl3 MFC. Chamber must be taken offline for MFC swap. 8. Perform 200 pump/purge cycles on the main chamber page before any maintenance access.
safety_requirements: BCl3 TLV-C: 1 ppm. Wear supplied-air respirator, chemical splash goggles, and acid/base gloves for any work near the gas cabinet. Confirm point-of-use toxic gas monitor (TGM) is active and showing GREEN before approaching. LOCKOUT/TAGOUT required before opening any gas line fittings.

title: BCl3 Flow TREND Response
procedure_steps: 1. Log trend alert: current bcl3_flow, direction, step, time to breach. Normal range 740–765 sccm. 2. Check BCl3 cylinder pressure. A steadily falling flow with fixed setpoint is a classic low-cylinder symptom. Schedule cylinder swap before pressure drops below 50 psi. 3. Review MFC calibration date in the PM log. If > 6 months since last calibration, request MFC verification. 4. If downward trend > 10 sccm over 3 consecutive wafers: escalate to ANOMALY response per SOP-BCL3-001. 5. Notify process engineer. Continue production if flow is within 5 sccm of lower limit with engineer approval only.
safety_requirements: Standard fab PPE. BCl3 gas system is sealed during normal tool operation. Do not approach gas cabinet without confirming TGM is GREEN.

title: Cl2 Flow Out-of-Range ANOMALY Response
procedure_steps: 1. Do NOT open chamber. Chlorine (Cl2) is a toxic oxidizer — TLV-TWA 0.5 ppm, IDLH 10 ppm. 2. Check cl2_flow reading: normal range is 748–758 sccm. 3. If flow is out of range in either direction: place lot on HOLD. Stop cassette loading. 4. Check loaded recipe set-point against approved master recipe. Recipe version mismatch is common after maintenance reloads. 5. Check Cl2 cylinder pressure at the gas cabinet VMB. If < 50 psi, cylinder changeover is required per gas changeover SOP. 6. If recipe and cylinder are correct: MFC fault suspected. Log MFC replacement request. Take chamber offline. 7. Before maintenance access: run 200 pump/purge cycles from Maintain/Main Chamber page. Verify chamber pressure at base (< 1×10⁻³ Pa) before venting. 8. After MFC replacement: run VAT valve Relearn Sequence (60 sccm Ar at 10 mTorr for VAT-64; 40 sccm Ar for VAT-65) before production restart.
safety_requirements: Cl2 TLV-TWA: 0.5 ppm, OSHA PEL: 1 ppm. Full-face respirator (SCBA or supplied air), chemical splash goggles, and PVC or neoprene gloves required for gas cabinet work. Confirm Cl2 toxic gas monitor at fab exhaust is active and alarming GREEN. Emergency: evacuate area, call EHS emergency line, do not re-enter until TGM reads < 0.5 ppm.

title: Cl2 Flow TREND Response
procedure_steps: 1. Log trend: current cl2_flow, direction, step, time to breach. Normal range 748–758 sccm. 2. Cl2 range is narrow (10 sccm). Any drift trend must be treated seriously — escalate to ANOMALY response per SOP-CL2-001 if drift rate exceeds 3 sccm over 2 wafers. 3. Check Cl2 cylinder pressure. 4. Review MFC calibration date. Cl2-MFC drift is a documented failure mode on the LAM 9600 TCP; long-term production data shows this as a leading cause of out-of-spec etch. 5. Notify process engineer. Do not continue production without engineer approval if flow is within 2 sccm of either limit.
safety_requirements: Standard fab PPE. Confirm Cl2 TGM is GREEN before approaching tool.

title: Chamber Pressure Out-of-Range ANOMALY Response
procedure_steps: 1. Check pressure reading: normal range 942–1420 mTorr. 2. If pressure > 1420 mTorr: high pressure increases ion scattering and reduces directionality. Place lot on HOLD. Check throttle valve position on Maintain/Pressure page. 3. If pressure < 942 mTorr: low pressure may cause plasma instability and arc faults. Stop cassette loading. Check for abnormal pump speed or gas flow drop. 4. Verify BCl3 and Cl2 flows are within normal range — pressure is directly coupled to gas flow. If flows are off, resolve gas fault first. 5. Check turbomolecular pump status LED and rpm. TMP rated at 1000 l/s; below-spec pump speed will cause high-pressure condition. 6. If throttle valve is suspected: check VAT valve position on the Maintain/Main Chamber page. Run VAT Relearn if position feedback is erratic. 7. Check for chamber leak: run a timed leak-rate test (vent load locks, close all valves, monitor CDG reading over 5 min). If leak rate > spec, identify and repair leak before resuming. 8. Escalate to process engineer if root cause not identified within 30 minutes.
safety_requirements: BCl3/Cl2 gas system remains pressurized during response. No chamber entry. Exhaust flow must remain active. LOCKOUT required before any vacuum pump or valve work.

title: Chamber Pressure TREND Response
procedure_steps: 1. Log trend: current pressure, direction, step, time to breach. Normal range 942–1420 mTorr. 2. If pressure is trending upward: check BCl3 and Cl2 flows for concurrent upward trends. Correlated gas+pressure rise indicates MFC or recipe issue. 3. If pressure trending upward with normal gas flows: throttle valve drift or TMP degradation suspected. Schedule PM inspection. 4. If pressure trending downward: check for increased pump speed or small gas flow reduction. Confirm CDG calibration is current. 5. Notify process engineer if time-to-breach < 3 wafers.
safety_requirements: Standard fab PPE. Exhaust system must remain active.

title: RF Bottom Power Out-of-Range ANOMALY Response
procedure_steps: 1. Check rf_btm_pwr reading: normal range 124–142 W. Bottom RF is capacitively coupled at 13.56 MHz; it controls ion energy (etch directionality) independently of TCP top power. 2. If rf_btm_pwr > 142 W: excess ion energy may cause photoresist erosion and sidewall damage. Place lot on HOLD. 3. If rf_btm_pwr < 124 W: insufficient bias may reduce etch directionality and cause footing. Stop cassette loading. 4. Check recipe set-point on the bottom RF generator page. A recipe version mismatch often explains a step-function power offset. 5. Check RF match unit status (auto-tune indicator). If the match unit is hunting (frequent re-tune), the RF cable or match network has a fault. 6. Check bottom RF generator hour counter. Replace or service at 1200 hours. 7. If match unit is confirmed faulty: take chamber offline. Bottom RF match unit replacement requires LOCKOUT and qualified RF technician.
safety_requirements: RF radiation hazard: do NOT operate with RF cable disconnected or shielding removed. Standard fab PPE for response. LOCKOUT required for any RF hardware access. BCl3/Cl2 exhaust must remain active.

title: RF Bottom Power TREND Response
procedure_steps: 1. Log trend: current rf_btm_pwr, direction, step, time to breach. Normal range 124–142 W. 2. Check RF generator hour counter. If > 1100 hours, schedule PM. 3. Review RF match unit auto-tune log for increased tuning frequency (early sign of network degradation). 4. If drift > 5 W over 3 wafers: escalate to ANOMALY response per SOP-RF-001. 5. Notify process engineer. Continue with increased sampling if within 3 W of limit with engineer approval.
safety_requirements: Standard fab PPE. RF shielding must remain intact.

title: Gas Leak or Toxic Gas Alarm — BCl3 or Cl2
procedure_steps: 1. IMMEDIATELY activate fab emergency stop for the 9600 tool. 2. Evacuate all personnel from the bay. Do not re-enter until cleared by EHS. 3. Call EHS emergency line. Report: tool ID (LAM 9600 TCP), suspected gas (BCl3 or Cl2), current production status. 4. Do NOT attempt to locate or repair the leak. Gas cabinet automatic shutoff will isolate the cylinder if TGM alarm is active. 5. Account for all personnel in the bay. Report headcount to EHS. 6. If Cl2: TLV-TWA is 0.5 ppm; IDLH is 10 ppm. Cl2 is a strong oxidizer — keep ignition sources away from the area. 7. If BCl3: TLV-C is 1 ppm. BCl3 reacts with atmospheric moisture to form HCl and boric acid — fire/water-based suppression may worsen exposure. 8. Resume production only after EHS clearance, confirmed TGM reading < TLV, and written authorization from EHS and process engineer.
safety_requirements: EMERGENCY SOP — supersedes all production priority. SCBA or supplied-air respirator required for re-entry. No entry without EHS escort and 4-gas monitor confirmation.
approver: EHS Manager and Site Safety Officer

title: Unplanned Chamber Shutdown and Safe-State Procedure
procedure_steps: 1. Press STOP on the system controller. The current wafer will complete its step; no new wafers will be loaded from the cassette. 2. If immediate abort is required (e.g., RED alarm active): select ABORT from the alarm screen. Process aborts and wafer is unloaded to load lock. 3. From the Maintain/Main Chamber page: run 200 pump/purge cycles to sweep residual BCl3/Cl2 from chamber. 4. Confirm chamber pressure < 1×10⁻³ Pa before any valve work. 5. Place tool in LOCKOUT state per LOCKOUT/TAGOUT procedure. Verify 208 VAC K1 contactor is de-energized and 24 VDC maintenance panel is tagged out. 6. Log the unplanned shutdown event in the MES with: fault type, last wafer processed, RF hours at shutdown, and action taken. 7. Do not restart tool without process engineer sign-off and a 5-wafer qualification run.
safety_requirements: LOCKOUT/TAGOUT per SEMI-S2 Guidelines before any chamber access. BCl3 and Cl2 gas lines remain pressurized at VMB until gas cabinet isolation — confirm gas cabinet is in STANDBY before proceeding. Electrical: 208 VAC 3-phase to K1 contactor; 24 VDC from DC panel — both must be tagged out.

title: Scheduled PM Trigger and Production Stop Procedure
procedure_steps: 1. PM is triggered by any of the following: RF generator hours > 1200, DSQ RF hours > 70, or calendar interval (quarterly). 2. At PM trigger: complete the current lot if all wafers are within spec. Do not start a new lot. 3. Log PC RF Hours and DSQ RF Hours from the Maintain/TCP page on the wet clean record sheet before shutdown. 4. Run HGS sweep (or 200 pump/purge cycles from Maintain/Main Chamber) before venting chamber for wet clean. 5. Wet clean procedure: reduce chamber heater to 35–40°C before opening. Soak chamber with DI water for one hour. 6. Clean in order: chamber walls → VAT valve (top and bottom) → o-ring grooves (1350 grit Diamond ScrubTIPS only) → manometers → removable parts. 7. Final IPA wipe: use fresh MiraWIPE for final pass — this is the most critical step for particle performance. 8. Replace quarterly PM items: VAT motor housing seals (Size 329), Nupro valve stem tips, Side Plate O-rings, DSQ O-rings (Outer Gas, Inner Gas, both Spacers, TCP Top & Bottom). 9. Replace at wet clean: Inner Door O-rings (part #205756) and End Point Window O-ring (Size 160). Replace DSQ TCP Window O-ring if DSQ RF hours > 70. 10. After reassembly: run 50 condition wafers and calibrate endpoint detectors before returning tool to production. 11. Run VAT Relearn Sequence after power-up: VAT-64 requires 60 sccm Ar at 10 mTorr; VAT-65 requires 40 sccm Ar.
safety_requirements: Full LOCKOUT/TAGOUT required before wet clean or any part replacement. DI water and IPA only — no solvents. Dirty DI water is chlorine-contaminated — dispose in hazardous waste collection tank. Watlow controller ramp-up after reassembly: 50°C → 100°C → 130°C ±5°C with stability verification at each step.
approver: Senior Process Engineer and Maintenance Lead

title: Wafer Hold and Lot Quarantine Procedure
procedure_steps: 1. When any sensor ANOMALY of severity HIGH or CRITICAL is detected: immediately place the affected wafer ID and entire lot on HOLD in the MES. 2. Mark affected cassette with a RED quarantine tag. Do not move cassette from elevator until QA disposition is complete. 3. Complete dump rinse on all etched wafers before resist strip — this step is mandatory regardless of fault type. If dump rinse is skipped, photoresist removal will be incomplete. 4. Notify QA Engineer with: lot ID, wafer ID range, chamber ID, fault sensor, deviation value, and process step number. 5. QA Engineer will determine disposition: rework, scrap, or accept with deviation. 6. Document all affected wafers in the NCR (Non-Conformance Report) system. 7. No lot may ship without QA Engineer sign-off on the NCR.
safety_requirements: Standard fab PPE. No additional safety hazard beyond normal tool operation.

title: Escalation to Process Engineer or Fab Manager
procedure_steps: 1. Escalate to process engineer immediately when: fault deviation > 30 W (TCP), > 15 sccm (BCl3/Cl2), or > 200 mTorr (pressure), OR 3+ consecutive wafers affected, OR CRITICAL severity alert triggered. 2. Escalate to fab manager when: process engineer is unreachable, gas leak or TGM alarm is active, or unplanned shutdown exceeds 2 hours. 3. When paging process engineer: provide tool ID (LAM 9600 TCP CHA/CHB), fault sensor, current value, normal range, number of wafers affected, and current lot ID. 4. Document all escalation events in the shift log with timestamp, contact name, and response time. 5. System MTTR target: < 4 hours from fault detection to production restart. If > 4 hours, escalate to fab manager and initiate downtime report.
safety_requirements: No additional hazard. Follow all active fault SOPs during escalation.
